title: La caponera
desc: Three wheels, no doors, and a price to agree first
setting: You are on a corner in the rain and a caponera pulls up beside you.

options.es: A la parada de buses. ¿Cuánto me cobra?
options.en: To the bus stop. How much will you charge me?
options.feedback: Destination and price in one breath. Settling the fare before you get in is the whole rule.
The destination is right. You have left the price for afterwards, which is where it goes wrong.

options.en: I do not know, you tell me.
options.feedback: Handing him the whole decision is how you end up paying double.

options.es: Ideay, está caro. ¿En ochenta me lleva?
options.en: Ideay, that is expensive. Will you take me for eighty?
options.feedback: Ideay takes the sting out and you named a counter-price. That is haggling as it is expected here.
He expected you to try. Taking the first number marks you out.

options.en: I am not paying you that.
options.feedback: Too hard. Haggling here is a game, not an accusation.
You met in the middle, which is exactly how it is supposed to end.
Agreed, and fine. Dale pues would have closed it warmer.
You have just argued yourself up to his price.

steps.speaker: Conductor
steps.es: Súbase pues. Agárrese que va mojado.
steps.en: Get in then. Hold on, it is wet.

options.feedback: Short, local, and gets you into the caponera.
Correct. Slightly stiff for a man who calls you jefe.
He will hear it as an instruction from somebody who does not trust him.
